ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a 9 V power supply; the upper end of the power supply is connected to the upper node through the top 2 kΩ resistor. This node divides downward into two branches: the right branch is a 1 kΩ resistor directly connected to the bottom common wire; the middle branch is a 1 kΩ resistor in series with diode VD and then connected to the bottom common wire. Reasoning: Let the voltage of the upper node relative to the bottom common wire be V. If diode VD conducts forward, the problem gives its forward voltage drop as 0.5 V. Then the middle diode-branch current is (V - 0.5)/1 kΩ, the right 1 kΩ branch current is V/1 kΩ, and the current flowing through the top 2 kΩ resistor into the node is (9 - V)/2 kΩ. Write KCL for the upper node: (9 - V)/2 kΩ = V/1 kΩ + (V - 0.5)/1 kΩ. Multiplying both sides by 2 kΩ gives: 9 - V = 2V + 2(V - 0.5) = 4V - 1, so 10 = 5V, V = 2 V. Therefore the current through VD is (2 - 0.5)/1 kΩ = 1.5 mA.

Let the top junction voltage be V relative to the bottom rail. From the text, take the forward drop of VD as 0.5 V, so if conducting the diode-branch current is (V - 0.5)/1 kΩ, while the right branch current is V/1 kΩ and the current through the 2 kΩ resistor is (9 - V)/2 kΩ. Apply KCL: (9 - V)/2 kΩ = V/1 kΩ + (V - 0.5)/1 kΩ. Solve for V = 2 V, then compute the diode current as (2 - 0.5)/1 kΩ = 1.5 mA.
